arxiv-1606-07126.title: Assessing the interactivity and prescriptiveness of faculty professional development workshops: The Real-Time Professional Development Observation Tool (R-PDOT)
arxiv-1606-07126.creator: Alice Olmstead, Chandra Turpen
arxiv-1606-07126.description: Abstract Professional development workshops are one of the primary mechanisms used to help faculty improve their teaching, and draw in many STEM instructors every year. Although workshops serve a critical role in changing instructional practices within our community, we rarely assess workshops through careful consideration of how they engage faculty.

arxiv-2108-11341.title: Driven quantum harmonic oscillators: A working medium for thermal machines
arxiv-2108-11341.creator: Heather Leitch, Nicolò Piccione, Bruno Bellomo, Gabriele De Chiara
arxiv-2108-11341.description: Abstract The study of quantum thermodynamics is key to the development of quantum thermal machines. In contrast to most of the previous proposals based on discrete strokes, here we consider a working substance that is permanently coupled to two or more baths at different temperatures and continuously driven.

arxiv-2202-08311.title: Single Trajectory Nonparametric Learning of Nonlinear Dynamics
arxiv-2202-08311.creator: Ingvar Ziemann, Henrik Sandberg, Nikolai Matni
arxiv-2202-08311.description: Abstract Given a single trajectory of a dynamical system, we analyze the performance of the nonparametric least squares estimator (LSE). More precisely, we give nonasymptotic expected l 2 l^{2} -distance bounds between the LSE and the true regression function, where expectation is evaluated on a fresh, counterfactual, trajectory.

arxiv-2210-00152.title: p ​ y py GWBSE: A high throughput workflow package for GW-BSE calculations
arxiv-2210-00152.creator: Tathagata Biswas, Arunima K. Singh
arxiv-2210-00152.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Tathagata Biswas, Arunima K. Singh. We develop an open-source python workflow package, py GWBSE to perform automated first-principles calculations within the GW-BSE (Bethe-Salpeter) framework. GW-BSE is a many body perturbation theory based approach to explore the quasiparticle (QP) and excitonic properties of materials. The GW approximation has proven to be effective in accurately predicting bandgaps of a wide range of materials by overcoming the bandgap underestimation issues of the more widely used density functional theory (DFT).

arxiv-2306-16407.description: Abstract Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes were introduced by Etzion and Silberstein in 2009. In their work, they proposed a conjecture on the largest dimension of a space of matrices over a finite field whose nonzero elements are supported on a given Ferrers diagram and all have rank lower bounded by a fixed positive integer d d .

Growing polarisation in society caught the attention of the scientific community as well as news media, which devote special issues to this phenomenon. arxiv-2404-07923.title: A Bayesian Estimator of Sample Size
arxiv-2404-07923.creator: Dehua Bi, Yuan Ji
arxiv-2404-07923.description: Abstract We consider a Bayesian estimator of sample size (BESS) and an application to oncology dose optimization clinical trials. BESS is built upon three pillars, S ample size of the experiment, E vidence from the observed data, and C onfidence in the posterior inference.

arxiv-2404-17139.title: A Central Pattern Generator Network for Simple Control of Gait Transitions in Hexapod Robots based on Phase Reduction
arxiv-2404-17139.creator: Norihisa Namura, Hiroya Nakao
arxiv-2404-17139.description: Abstract We present a model of the central pattern generator (CPG) network that can control gait transitions in hexapod robots in a simple manner based on phase reduction. The CPG network consists of six weakly coupled limit-cycle oscillators, whose synchronization dynamics can be described by six phase equations through phase reduction.

arxiv-2410-17950.title: Benchmarking Floworks against OpenAI & Anthropic: A Novel Framework for Enhanced LLM Function Calling
arxiv-2410-17950.creator: Nirav Bhan, Shival Gupta, Sai Manaswini, Ritik Baba, Narun Yadav, Hillori Desai, Yash Choudhary, Aman Pawar, Sarthak Shrivastava, Sudipta Biswas
arxiv-2410-17950.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown remarkable capabilities in various domains, yet their economic impact has been limited by challenges in tool use and function calling. This paper introduces ThorV2, a novel architecture that significantly enhances LLMs’ function calling abilities.

pmc-12358506.title: Assessing resilience in pharmacy education during the COVID-19 era
pmc-12358506.creator: Asmaa Al-Haqan, Ian Bates, Mona Almanasef, Dalia Bajis, Saja A. Alnahar
pmc-12358506.description: In higher education, resilience is vital for enabling students and academics to confront challenges and sustain well-being. This study aimed to explore resilience in pharmacy higher education within the Eastern Mediterranean Region.

pmc-12569636.description: Co-variation with functionally integrated sensory structures contributes to the size evolution of brain regions. pmc-13046048.creator: Esmaeil Mehrara, Mariam Mohamed, Martijn Van-Essen, Jesus Lopez Urdaneta
pmc-13046048.description: Positron Emission Tomography Response Criteria in Solid Tumors (PERCIST) quantifies changes in radiotracer uptake to assess therapeutic response in cancer. However, the accuracy of these quantifications depends on imaging parameters, tumor size, and the local tumor-to-background uptake ratio (local-TBR). In this study, ‘background’ refers to the surroundings of the lesion rather than a standardized reference tissue.

pmc-13320049.title: Mechanics and mechanobiology of arterial development
pmc-13320049.creator: Jay D Humphrey, Erica L Schwarz
pmc-13320049.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Arteries serve primarily a biomechanical function. Critical insight into arterial structure, properties, and function thus derives from knowledge of mechanosensitive gene expression, associated microstructural organization, and biomechanical metrics such as compliance and vasoactive capacity. This review focuses on time-course changes in hemodynamic loads and associated changes in the transcriptional profile, mural composition, overall geometry, and mechanical properties of arteries during postnatal development, namely, from birth to a healthy adult.

Typhimurium), yiiD encodes a two‐domain protein, with one domain having bona fide malonyl‐ACP decarboxylase activity, and the other showing sequence similarity to Gcn5‐type acetyltransferases (GNATs). Recent work on this enzyme was motivated by the essentiality of its decarboxylase domain to initiation of fatty acid biosynthesis in a strain devoid of β‐ketoacyl‐[acyl‐carrier‐protein, ACP] synthase III (FabH) activity. A function for the putative GNAT domain has not been established.
